title: A Friend's Observation
content:
Sneha stood frozen.

The words "my love" echoed repeatedly in her mind.

A strange feeling spread through her heart.

Jealousy.

Confusion.

Disappointment.

She tried not to show it on her face, but her smile had already begun to fade.

Meanwhile, Siddu continued speaking on the phone.

A cheerful laugh came from the other end.

"So, I heard you're in Shimla," the voice said. "Why don't you come over to my place for lunch?"

Siddu smiled.

"I'd love to."

He paused for a moment before adding,

"But... I have a friend with me."

"A friend?"

"Yeah."

"...A girl."

There was complete silence.

Then suddenly the person on the other end burst into laughter.

"Hold on... are you seriously traveling with a girl?"

Siddu laughed softly.

"Yeah. She's a really good friend."

"Now I'm definitely curious. Bring her along too."

"Alright. We'll be there soon."

The call ended.

Sneha, who had been quietly waiting, finally asked,

"Who was that?"

Siddu smiled.

"My best friend."

She hesitated before asking another question.

"The one you called... 'my love'?"

Siddu couldn't help laughing.

"Oh, that."

"He and I have been best friends since our B.Tech days. We were so close that everyone used to joke we were like a couple."

"He loves teasing me."

The heaviness in Sneha's heart melted away almost instantly.

A small smile slowly returned to her face.

"What's his name?"

"Yashwanth."

"He lives here in Shimla. He invited both of us for lunch."

Siddu looked at her.

"Would you like to come?"

Sneha nodded with a smile.

"I'd love to."

About half an hour later, the cab stopped in front of a beautiful house surrounded by tall pine trees.

Before they could ring the bell, the front door opened.

A cheerful young man stepped outside.

The moment his eyes met Siddu's...

Both of them smiled.

Without saying a word, they walked toward each other and shared a warm hug.

"It's been too long," Yashwanth said.

"It has," Siddu replied.

Yashwanth then turned toward Sneha.

"So, you're Sneha."

He smiled warmly.

"Welcome."

"Thank you," Sneha replied politely.

After exchanging a few more words, the three of them entered the house.

Sneha excused herself to wash her face.

The moment she disappeared into the washroom, Yashwanth immediately turned toward Siddu with a mischievous grin.

"So..."

Siddu already knew what was coming.

"What?"

"Are my eyes deceiving me?"

Siddu sighed.

"What do you mean?"

"I never thought I'd see the day when Siddharth would actually spend time with a girl."

He chuckled.

"After... everything that happened."

Siddu's smile slowly faded.

"Let's not talk about that."

Yashwanth immediately understood.

"Sorry."

Then Siddu smiled again.

"Just one request."

"Hmm?"

"Please don't tease me in front of Sneha."

Yashwanth grinned.

"No promises."

Both of them laughed.

A few minutes later, Sneha returned, and the three of them sat down for lunch.

The atmosphere quickly became cheerful.

Yashwanth kept everyone laughing with his jokes while Siddu occasionally joined in, something Sneha hadn't expected to see.

She had always seen Siddu carrying sadness in his eyes.

Seeing him laugh so freely made her genuinely happy.

As lunch continued, Yashwanth quietly observed Sneha.

The way she looked at Siddu...

The way she smiled whenever he spoke...

The way she unconsciously paid attention to every little thing about him...

Something caught his attention.

After a while, Sneha excused herself to wash her hands.

The moment she left the dining table, Yashwanth leaned closer.

"Siddu."

"Hmm?"

"Are you absolutely sure... you two are just friends?"

Siddu looked at him in confusion.

"Of course."

"What made you ask that?"

Yashwanth smiled knowingly.

"Nothing."

He glanced toward the washroom.

"It's just..."

"The way she looks at you doesn't seem like ordinary friendship."

For the first time...

Siddu became silent.

Those words lingered in his mind.

Just then, Sneha returned.

The conversation ended immediately.

But Yashwanth's question...

Stayed with Siddu long after lunch was over.

For the first time since meeting Sneha, Siddu found himself replaying every moment they had spent together.

Had Yashwanth noticed something that he himself had failed to see?

The question quietly settled into his mind...

Refusing to leave.
